# Plan (opus, strong)

**Goal.** All four pure crates' `clippy.toml` files get the same 55 new entries. Together they close the remaining impure doors in std: the rest of `std::fs`, `Path`'s methods that touch the disk, the environment and the command line, stdin/stdout/stderr, the network, processes, threads and `RandomState`. The sanctioned exceptions stay free. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` stays green: each of the 4 existing hits gets an item-level `allow` that says why. Two new acceptance tests guard the lint: one fails when the four files differ, the other runs clippy over a fixture with one use per entry, so every entry is shown to fire. The second test matters because the planner checked that clippy only *warns* about an entry it cannot resolve ("does not refer to a reachable function"), even under `-D warnings`.
